The very long conductivity-dependent part of the candidate is exactly the real and imaginary decomposition of the compact generalized Drude-Smith expression σ̃(ω) = (sigma/S) Σ_{n=0}^{12} c_n/(1 - i x)^(n+1). Its real part contains the polynomials 1 - x², 1 - 3x², 1 - 6x² + x⁴, and so forth. These are not independently inferred mechanisms: they are the even-binomial terms in Re[(1 + i x)^(n+1)]. Likewise, the second sequence containing 2, 3 - x², 4 - 4x², and the higher-order patterns consists of the odd-binomial terms in Im[(1 + i x)^(n+1)]/x. Thus every polynomial through twelfth order follows automatically from the same known rational response function. The divisor S merely converts the usual Drude conductivity prefactor into the prescribed measured zero-frequency conductivity, ensuring σ̃(0) = sigma. The outer expression is also established electrodynamics. If σ1 = Re σ̃ and σ2 = Im σ̃, the candidate attenuation coefficient is α = sqrt[(ω mu/2)(sqrt(σ1² + (ω epsilon - σ2)²) - (ω epsilon - σ2))], and E_env = E_0 exp(-αz). This is the standard homogeneous-medium propagation constant evaluated with a complex, frequency-dependent conductivity. It reduces to the supplied classical baseline when the conductivity is effectively real and frequency independent. Generalized Drude-Smith conductivity, including its formal sum over post-collision memory coefficients, is already present in the open scientific literature; retaining twelve terms is simply a finite truncation of that known series. The exact fully expanded twelfth-order string is unlikely to be printed verbatim in a textbook because it is unnecessarily long, but it is uniquely and mechanically recoverable from the standard compact formula using binomial expansion. Its apparent complexity therefore does not constitute a new composite physical mechanism. Experimental data would be needed to fit the relaxation time and memory coefficients, but not to discover this functional form. Consequently, the complete equation is a predictable composition of established Maxwell attenuation and generalized Drude-Smith response rather than a scientifically novel data-inferred law.
